label: input token j at original positions 0-2
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is j at one of the first three original-phase steps (t = 0, 1, 2); precision 1.0 and recall ~1.0 on dev. Magnitude depends on position: about 1.0x max at t=0, about 0.95x at t=1, and about 0.3-0.4x at t=2 (t=2 holds 16% of mass despite a third of the activations). It does not fire on j at t >= 3, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The only exceptions are 13 tiny activations (<0.05x max) on copy-phase j re-inputs.

issues: None of these are systematic. On test: precision 1.0, recall 0.99976, F1 0.99988, mass recall 0.99998. The predicate produced 0 false positives.

There were 12 misses on test, holding 0.0% of the activation mass. All are tiny (0.02-0.10x max) and sit on copy-phase j re-inputs: on dev the copy phase has 13 active steps out of 2.73M. So 'does not fire in the copy phase' holds approximately but is not literally true. The explanation already mentions these misses.

The magnitude claims fit the dev profile. Mass share is 0.433 / 0.411 / 0.156 at t=0 / 1 / 2, with roughly equal active counts (16441 / 16512 / 16768). That puts t=2 at about 0.35x the t=0 magnitude, and t=1 at about 0.95x.
Firing outside the predicate is essentially zero: 0 activations on the delimiter, 0 at orig_idx >= 3, 0 on any input token other than j. The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
